text.p: Australian building materials analysts said on Friday they plan to downgrade their 1996/97 earnings forecasts for Pioneer International Ltd due to the poor first quarter performance and the outlook for the current year.
"I think you will see a series of downgrades," one Sydney based analyst told Reuters.
Pioneer reported a pre-abnormal net profit after preference dividends of A$252.2 million for the yera to June 30, 1996.
"For the group as a whole we expect profitability in the current year to be materially below last year's record result," chief executive John Schubert told the annual meeting on Friday.
Pioneer said there was a substantial reduction in first quarter profitability from its petroleum arm, while the perfromance of its building materials arm was flat.

Fabian Babich, a building materials analyst at brokers ABN AMRO, said he was revising down his Pioneer 1996/97 earnings estimate to around A$240 million, but this was to be finalised from a previous forecast of A$254 million.
"The real uncertainty is how much it (overall profit) is going to be down," Babich told Reuters.
Analysts said the problem was in the petroleum business rather than in Pioneer's core building materials opertaions.
ANZ Securities building materials analyst Sean Cooney said he had revised down his 1996/97 profit estimates to around A$213 million/A$214 million from A$239 million perviously.

Cooney told Reuters the cut in forecast had come from the petroleum division. Pioneer jointly owns Australia's largest petroleum retail and refining group, Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd, which trades as Ampol, with Caltex Australia Ltd.

One Melbourne-based building materials analyst said: "I think if things stay the way they are we could see no dividend coming from that (petroleum) business." Pioneer received a A$69.5 million dividend from Ampol in the 1995/96 year.
The Melbourne analyst said on a worst-case scenario for the petroleum business Pioneer's 1996/97 pre-abnormal net profit before preference dividends would be as low as A$211 million.
However, he added he had recently downgraded his Pioneer earnings estimate to A$232 million from A$247 million.
BT Securities building materials analyst Chris Haynes said he had recently downgraded his Pioneer forecast for the current year to A$232 million from the A$247 million previously.
Pioneer shares ended 12 cents or 3.3 percent lower at A$3.43 on a volume of 2.98 million shares on Friday.
